title: Customer portal database connection pool exhaustion
description: The Customer portal (site_id 1002) is intermittently returning HTTP 500 responses during periods of elevated traffic. Application logs show repeated connection acquisition timeouts from the PostgreSQL connection pool, followed by successful requests once existing connections are released. The database remains reachable and accepts direct connections, but the application frequently reaches its configured connection limit. The issue is concentrated on requests that load customer account history, where several database queries remain active for significantly longer than normal. Investigation should compare active database sessions against application pool metrics, identify queries holding connections for extended periods, and determine whether slow queries, connection leaks, or insufficient pool sizing are contributing to the exhaustion. Restarting affected application instances provides temporary relief, but the underlying connection usage should be investigated before simply increasing the pool size.

title: Corporate website large file uploads failing
description: The Corporate website (site_id 1001) accepts small file uploads normally but consistently fails when users submit files larger than approximately 50 MB. The application returns a generic upload error after several minutes, while server logs indicate that the multipart upload session is terminated before the final parts are transferred. Connectivity to the storage backend is stable and smaller multipart uploads complete successfully. The failure threshold appears to correspond with the configured request body limit and reverse-proxy timeout rather than a storage-provider outage. Investigation should check upload-size and timeout settings at the CDN, reverse proxy, web application, and storage-client layers. It should also be determined whether large files are streamed or buffered in application memory. As a temporary workaround, users can split large uploads into smaller files while the request limits and timeout configuration are reviewed.

closed.message: Uploads above the documented 50 MB limit are rejected on purpose.

title: Online store checkout failing for part of the traffic
description: Since this morning roughly a third of checkout attempts on the Online store (Site 1005) end with a generic 'Payment could not be processed' page. The rest of the shop (browsing, cart, account pages) works. Customers are contacting support and some retry several times. Release 2.14 of the store backend went out yesterday evening (new order-history export, upgraded ORM library). Initial suspicion is the payment gateway.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: Opened a ticket with the payment gateway vendor - pretty sure it is on their side, the error page is the one we show when the gateway call fails.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: Gateway status page is green and the vendor says our merchant account shows normal volume and no declines on their side. Our own logs show the failures happen BEFORE we call the gateway: 'TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 20 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00'.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: DB server itself looks fine: CPU 35%, no lock waits above 1s, 38 active connections out of 300 allowed. So the database is not the bottleneck - the app's own pool is.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: Error rate jumps every hour at :00 for ~10 minutes, then drops to ~5%. The new order-history export from 2.14 is scheduled hourly at :00 and runs inside the web workers.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: Restarted all 4 web workers at 11:05. Errors dropped to almost zero, then came back at 12:00 exactly.

comments.author: admin
comments.text: Rollback to 2.13 is possible but would also revert the ORM upgrade, which fixed a security advisory. Not keen on rolling back the whole release. Can we disable just the export?

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: There is no feature flag for the export. It is wired into the scheduler at startup. Also noticed the ORM upgrade changed the default pool size from 50 to 20 - our config never set it explicitly.

title: Customer portal users randomly logged out
description: Users of the Customer portal (Site 1002) report being logged out in the middle of their work, sometimes several times an hour, and losing unsaved forms. Sessions are stored in the shared Redis cache cluster, which other services also use. No deploy to the portal in the last week.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: Could not reproduce on my machine. Asked support for browser details of affected users.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: Every report support forwarded is from Chrome. Looks like a Chrome cookie issue - maybe the SameSite change in the latest version?

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: Reproduced it twice on Firefox this morning, so it is not Chrome-specific. Both times the session cookie was still present in the browser, but the server no longer knew the session id.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: Redis INFO: used_memory is at maxmemory (4 GB), maxmemory-policy is allkeys-lru, evicted_keys grows by ~1,200 per minute during business hours.

comments.author: admin
comments.text: The analytics team started caching report results in the same Redis cluster on Monday. Not sure how much space that takes.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: Logouts cluster between 09:00 and 11:00 and again around 14:00, which matches when analytics refresh their dashboards.

title: Nightly data warehouse load fails with 'No space left on device' again
description: The nightly ETL that loads sales data into the data warehouse failed again last night with 'OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device' on the ETL server's /data volume (500 GB). This is the third time in about a month. Each time it was 'fixed' by deleting old files and re-running the job manually. Morning sales reports are missing until the job is re-run.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: History: same error 31 days ago and 19 days ago. Both times tech1 cleared /data/tmp (about 180 GB each time) and re-ran the job; closed as Resolved.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: /data is 100% full again. /data/tmp holds 2,140 files named etl_stage_*.parquet, the oldest from 18 days ago. The job is supposed to delete its staging files when it finishes.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: The cleanup step runs only on success. When the job fails half-way (e.g. the source DB times out), the staging files are left behind and the next night adds a new set on top. Last month's ETL logs show 6 partial failures on source-DB timeouts.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: There is also a weekly cron job that cleans /data/tmp, but it only deletes files older than 30 days, so it never catches up.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: Cleared /data/tmp again (176 GB freed) and re-ran the load. Finished at 09:42, reports are back. Not closing this yet since it will obviously come back.

comments.author: tech3

comments.author: tech1

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: Don't know yet, I don't have access to the mail service dashboard. Waiting for someone who does.

title: Burst of failed logins on the Internal HR portal
description: The Internal HR portal (Site 1007) recorded about 40,000 failed login attempts in the last 6 hours, against a normal level of a few hundred per day. The attempts target many different usernames. Two accounts were locked out and one contractor account logged in successfully from an unfamiliar country. MFA is enforced for employees but not yet for contractor accounts.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: Attempts come from ~3,000 different IP addresses, mostly residential ranges, 1-15 attempts per IP. Usernames look like they come from an old leaked list - about 30% of them don't exist in our directory.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: The successful contractor login (user c.levi) was at 04:12 from an IP in a country where we have no staff. The session downloaded 3 payslip PDFs, then nothing. The contractor says they were asleep.

comments.author: admin
comments.text: Disabled c.levi and killed their active sessions. Rate limiting on the login page is per IP only, which is why the spread across many IPs gets through.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: WAF can add a challenge (CAPTCHA) after 3 failures per username, but enabling it needs a change request with HR's sign-off - they worry it will confuse non-technical staff.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: Attempts still going, about 5,000 per hour now. Checked: no other successful logins from new countries since 04:12.

title: Status page shows all green during a real API slowdown
description: Between 13:10 and 13:55 today, partners reported API responses taking 8-20 seconds and some timeouts, but the Status page (Site 1009) showed every component as Operational the whole time. Partners are now asking why our status page cannot be trusted.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: The status page component 'Public API' is driven by a synthetic check that calls GET /api/health every minute. That endpoint returned 200 in under 50 ms throughout the incident.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: /api/health only checks that the web process is up - it does not touch the database or the downstream services, and it is served from the CDN edge cache with a 60s TTL.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: Root cause of the slowdown itself was a slow query after an index was dropped by a migration; that part is already fixed (index restored at 13:52). This fault is only about the status page not reflecting it.

comments.author: admin
comments.text: The status page vendor also supports a 'degraded' state based on a latency threshold, but we never configured one. Partners have a 99.5% availability SLA with a 5s response-time definition.

title: Partner extranet file imports silently dropping rows
description: Partners upload daily CSV files to the Partner extranet (Site 1003) over SFTP. Since about a week ago, some partners say products and contacts they uploaded are missing in the extranet. The import job reports success every day, with no errors.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: Compared one partner's file with what was imported: 1,204 rows in the file, 1,151 imported. The import log says 'Processed 1151 rows, 0 errors'.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: All 53 missing rows contain non-English characters (accents, Hebrew, umlauts) in the name or address fields, e.g. 'Müller GmbH'.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: The SFTP/import server got an OS upgrade 8 days ago. The default locale changed from en_US.UTF-8 to POSIX. The import script opens files without an explicit encoding.

comments.author: tech2
comments.text: The script wraps the row parsing in try/except and 'continue's on any exception - that is why errors are 0. The bare except was added years ago to skip header lines.

comments.author: admin
comments.text: Partners keep their files for 30 days, so we can still re-import the affected week if we fix it soon.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: One partner says their file is UTF-16, not UTF-8. Not sure if that's true for others.

title: Payroll overtime miscalculated after the clock change
description: Payslip previews in the Payroll system (Site #1008) show wrong overtime for shifts that crossed the night of the daylight saving time change. Some employees are shown one hour too much overtime, others one hour too little. The monthly payroll run is scheduled in 2 days and cannot easily be corrected after payment.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: Affected: 112 employees, all with night shifts on the DST weekend. Day shifts are correct.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: This is an app bug - shift duration is calculated as end_time - start_time on local wall-clock times, so a shift over the clock change comes out one hour off.

comments.author: admin
comments.text: The payroll vendor says the software handles DST correctly if the time zone setting is right, and that our tenant is configured as 'UTC+2 (fixed)' instead of the named time zone. They blame configuration, not code.

comments.author: tech3
comments.text: Checked the tenant settings: time zone is indeed 'UTC+2 (fixed)'. It has been like that since the 2017 setup. But last year's DST change did not cause complaints, as far as anyone remembers.

comments.author: tech1
comments.text: Last year the clocks changed on a weekend with almost no night shifts (the plant was closed for maintenance), so it may simply not have been noticed.

comments.author: admin
comments.text: Changing the tenant time zone now will recalculate ALL historical shifts in the current period, according to the vendor docs. Payroll team is nervous about that two days before the run.
